qe: During the 19th century, a regressive social custom under the name of 'Kulinism' heavily degraded the position of women through institutionalized polygamy and mismatched marriages. This system was predominantly prevalent in which region of India?
qh: 19वीं शताब्दी के दौरान, 'कुलीनवाद' (Kulinism) नाम से प्रचलित एक प्रतिगामी सामाजिक प्रथा ने संस्थागत बहुविवाह और बेमेल विवाहों के माध्यम से महिलाओं की स्थिति को भारी ठेस पहुँचाई। यह व्यवस्था मुख्य रूप से भारत के किस क्षेत्र में प्रचलित थी?
o: Bengal
Madras Presidency
Punjab
Maharashtra
e: Detailed Explanation: In 19th-century Bengal, under the social system of Kulinism, highly exploitative forms of polygamy were practiced. Under this custom, even elderly men belonging to upper castes married very young girls, often leaving them abandoned or destitute, which severely degraded the overall position of women.

qe: Which prominent early socio-religious reformer explicitly challenged orthodox clerical groups by condemning the practice of Sati as a 'murder according to every shastra'?
qh: किस प्रमुख प्रारंभिक सामाजिक-धार्मिक सुधारक ने सती प्रथा की स्पष्ट रूप से 'प्रत्येक शास्त्र के अनुसार हत्या' के रूप में निंदा करके रूढ़िवादी लिपिकीय समूहों को चुनौती दी थी?
o: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
Raja Rammohan Roy
Dayanand Saraswati
Mahadev Govind Ranade
e: Detailed Explanation: Raja Rammohan Roy was the pioneering reformer of modern India who led a historic campaign against the practice of Sati. He used scriptural analysis to fight orthodox opposition, explicitly stating that the forced immolation of widows was nothing short of a 'murder according to every shastra'.

qe: The rigid stratification and social segregation associated with the caste system in modern India created major barriers against which democratic development?
qh: आधुनिक भारत में जाति व्यवस्था से जुड़े कड़े स्तरीकरण और सामाजिक अलगाव ने किस लोकतांत्रिक विकास के खिलाफ प्रमुख बाधाएं पैदा कीं?
o: The growth of a united national feeling and democratic spirit
The introduction of land revenue collection frameworks
The establishing of cross-border maritime trading networks
The direct legal translation of Western scientific texts
e: Detailed Explanation: The rigid caste system in India checked social mobility, checked individual initiative, and splintered society into numerous fragmented groups based on ritual status. In modern times, this fragmentation became a major structural obstacle to the development of a united national feeling and the spread of democracy.

qe: The dissemination of colonial culture and ideology as the dominant current by British rule triggered a reactive cultural movement among 19th-century Indian intellectuals. This response was characterized by:
qh: ब्रिटिश शासन द्वारा औपनिवेशिक संस्कृति और विचारधारा के प्रसार ने 19वीं शताब्दी के भारतीय बुद्धिजीवियों के बीच एक प्रतिक्रियात्मक सांस्कृतिक आंदोलन को जन्म दिया। इस प्रतिक्रिया की विशेषता क्या थी?
o: An immediate and total legal conversion to Western religious practices
An attempt to reinvigorate traditional institutions and realize the potential of traditional culture
The total abandonment of scriptural studies across all local languages
A spontaneous mass migration toward non-colonized European territories
e: Detailed Explanation: Faced with the challenge of an intrusive colonial culture and ideology, enlightened Indian thinkers did not blindly accept Westernization. Instead, they sought to reinvigorate traditional institutions, purge them of social evils, and realize the true reforming potential of traditional culture.

qe: What primary realization catalyzed the shared conviction among English-educated Indian youth in the late 19th century to reform their own socio-religious structures?
qh: 19वीं शताब्दी के उत्तरार्ध में अंग्रेजी-शिक्षित भारतीय युवाओं के बीच अपने स्वयं के सामाजिक-धार्मिक ढांचों में सुधार करने के साझा विश्वास को किस प्राथमिक अहसास ने प्रेरित किया?
o: The awareness that India was colonized due to internal weaknesses within its own social structure and culture
The absolute lack of rich mineral reservoirs in the sub-Himalayan zones
The dynamic degradation of linear agricultural productivity indices
The sudden structural breakdown of natural wildlife biomes
e: Detailed Explanation: The impact of modern Western ideas and the reality of defeat by a foreign power made educated Indians introspect. They realized that a vast country like India had been colonized by a handful of foreigners primarily because of deep structural weaknesses, superstitions, and social fragmentation within the Indian society and culture, which highlighted the urgent need for internal reform.

qe: During the 19th century, social reformers initially linked social movements directly with religious reforms. What was the primary reason for this close structural linkage?
qh: 19वीं शताब्दी के दौरान, सामाजिक सुधारकों ने शुरू में सामाजिक आंदोलनों को सीधे धार्मिक सुधारों से जोड़ा। इस करीबी संरचनात्मक जुड़ाव का प्राथमिक कारण क्या था?
o: Nearly all social ills like untouchability and gender inequality derived institutional legitimacy from religion
The colonial government mandated that all social changes must be cleared by religious bodies
Indian languages lacked secular terms to propagate ideas to the lower strata of society
The early upper-class reformers aimed to establish a new monotheistic state religion legally
e: Detailed Explanation: Social reform movements were initially tied to religion because major social evils, including untouchability and gender-based discrimination, derived their validation, authority, and structural legitimacy from misinterpreted religious traditions and scriptures.

qe: Which of the following organizations was among the earliest institutional setups instrumental in spearheading social reforms in India before the national movement took over leadership in the 20th century?
qh: 20वीं शताब्दी में राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन द्वारा नेतृत्व संभालने से पहले, भारत में सामाजिक सुधारों का नेतृत्व करने में सहायक शुरुआती संस्थागत सेटअपों में से कौन सा संगठन शामिल था?
o: The Indian National Social Conference
The All India Scheduled Castes Federation
The Congress Khilafat Swaraj Party
The Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha
e: Detailed Explanation: In the initial stages, localized organizations such as the Indian National Social Conference, the Servants of India Society, Christian missionaries, and enlightened individuals laid the foundation for social reform long before the Indian National Congress adopted it on a mass scale.

qe: To effectively reach and mobilize the masses, 19th-century socio-religious reformers primarily relied on which communicative tool?
qh: जनता तक प्रभावी ढंग से पहुँचने और उन्हें लामबंद करने के लिए, 19वीं शताब्दी के सामाजिक-धार्मिक सुधारक मुख्य रूप से किस संचार साधन पर निर्भर थे?
o: English-only political pamphlets distributed to the intelligentsia
Indian vernacular languages propagated through literature, press, and drama
Direct legal appeals filed inside the Federal Privy Council channels
Spontaneous radio broadcasts managed from non-colonial European centers
e: Detailed Explanation: Reformers recognized that westernized media was confined to the upper classes. To penetrate the lower strata, they actively used Indian vernacular languages and multiple formats—novels, dramas, poetry, short stories, and the local press.

qe: The comprehensive agenda of the early socio-religious reform movements in India was fundamentally anchored on which two-point core objective?
qh: भारत में शुरुआती सामाजिक-धार्मिक सुधार आंदोलनों का व्यापक एजेंडा मुख्य रूप से किन दो बिंदुओं के मुख्य उद्देश्य पर आधारित था?
o: Betterment of the status of women and removal of disabilities arising out of untouchability
The absolute expansion of private land sales and total abolition of local panchayats
Promoting Western dress codes and implementing English-only educational test metrics
Securing military representations for native intermediate castes inside colonial setups
e: Detailed Explanation: Although the reform movements covered many diverse aspects, their core agenda focused on two major areas: improving the status and rights of women in society, and eliminating the disabilities arising from untouchability.

qe: In the 19th century, Muslim women under Islamic legal traditions possessed what specific property right compared to their contemporary Hindu counterparts?
qh: 19वीं शताब्दी में, इस्लामी कानूनी परंपराओं के तहत मुस्लिम महिलाओं के पास उनकी समकालीन हिंदू महिलाओं की तुलना में कौन सा विशिष्ट संपत्ति का अधिकार था?
o: They could inherit property, but only half as much as men could
They enjoyed complete absolute equality with men in inheriting full agricultural holdings
They were legally barred from owning any physical real estate asset entirely
They could inherit property only if they terminated their existing marriage lines
e: Detailed Explanation: Unlike 19th-century Hindu women who lacked the right to inherit property, Muslim women could inherit property under Islamic law. However, gender inequality remained, as they were legally entitled to inherit only half as much share as men could.

qe: Social reformers actively targeted reforms in the domestic sphere, arguing that a radical change in the household was essential because:
qh: सामाजिक सुधारकों ने घरेलू क्षेत्र (domestic sphere) में सुधारों को सक्रिय रूप से लक्षित किया, यह तर्क देते हुए कि घर में आमूल-चूल परिवर्तन आवश्यक था क्योंकि:
o: The initial socialization of individuals takes place in the home, where women play a crucial role
The colonial government offered financial subsidies only to reformed households
The domestic sphere was the primary source of state agricultural tax collections
They aimed to completely eliminate traditional family structures in favor of Western systems
e: Detailed Explanation: Reformers understood that the domestic sphere is where the initial socialization of individuals occurs. Because women play a central role in rearing children, transforming the domestic environment was seen as key to shaping reformed citizens.

qe: When launching a frontal attack against the practice of Sati, Raja Rammohan Roy and his followers used which argument to strengthen their appeal?
qh: सती प्रथा के खिलाफ मोर्चा खोलते समय राजा राममोहन राय और उनके अनुयायियों ने अपने आह्वान को मजबूत करने के लिए किस तर्क का इस्तेमाल किया?
o: They argued that true religion and scriptures did not sanction an inferior status or forced death for women
They appealed to the financial benefits that British landlords would gain from widow estates
They stated that the practice was imported recently from non-Asian colonial systems
They advocated that the custom should be restricted strictly to lower castes
e: Detailed Explanation: To counter orthodox opposition, Raja Rammohan Roy turned to scripture. He argued from a rationalist perspective that the true, uncorrupted core of religion did not support an inferior status or the forced immolation of widows, describing it as a violation of human dignity.

qe: The historic anti-Sati regulation enacted under Lord William Bentinck, which declared the custom illegal and punishable as culpable homicide, was formally designated as:
qh: लॉर्ड विलियम बेंटिक के तहत अधिनियमित ऐतिहासिक सती-विरोधी नियम, जिसने इस प्रथा को अवैध और आपराधिक मानव वध के रूप में दंडनीय घोषित किया, उसे औपचारिक रूप से क्या कहा गया था?
o: Regulation XVII, A.D. 1829 of the Bengal Code
Bengal Infanticide Restriction Act of 1795
Native Civil Marriage Act of 1872
Age of Consent Code, 1891
e: Detailed Explanation: The practice was declared illegal and punishable by criminal courts as culpable homicide under Regulation XVII, A.D. 1829 of the Bengal Code. Initially applicable to the Bengal Presidency, it was extended to Madras and Bombay in 1830.

qe: In 1870, the colonial government passed a specific legislative Act targeting the secret practice of female infanticide. What did this Act make compulsory for parents?
qh: 1870 में, औपनिवेशिक सरकार ने कन्या भ्रूण हत्या/शिशु हत्या की गुप्त प्रथा को लक्षित करते हुए एक विशिष्ट अधिनियम पारित किया। इस अधिनियम ने माता-पिता के लिए क्या अनिवार्य कर दिया?
o: The mandatory registration of the birth of all babies and subsequent verification of female infants
The compulsory enrollment of all female children into Christian missionary boarding facilities
Paying a direct metabolic tax surcharge to the local district revenue collectorate
Surrendering ownership of all ancestral property to female heirs immediately
e: Detailed Explanation: To combat female infanticide practiced in secrecy among certain upper classes, the Female Infanticide Prevention Act of 1870 made it compulsory for parents to register all births and introduced verification checks on female infants for several years.

qe: The enactment of the landmark Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856, which legalised widow remarriage and legitimized their issues, was primarily due to the relentless efforts of which scholar?
qh: ऐतिहासिक हिंदू विधवा पुनर्विवाह अधिनियम, 1856 का पारित होना, जिसने विधवा विवाह को वैध बनाया, मुख्य रूप से किस विद्वान के अथक प्रयासों के कारण हुआ था?
o: Pandit Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
Raja Rammohan Roy
Karsondas Mulji
Professor D.K. Karve
e: Detailed Explanation: Pandit Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, serving as the principal of Sanskrit College in Calcutta, led the campaign for widow remarriage. He famously cited Vedic texts to prove to the orthodox community that Hindu traditions originally permitted the practice.

qe: Who among the following reformers established the specialized journal 'Satya Prakash' in Gujarati in 1852 to advocate for the right of widow remarriage?
qh: निम्नलिखित सुधारकों में से किसने विधवा पुनर्विवाह के अधिकार की वकालत करने के लिए 1852 में गुजराती में 'सत्य प्रकाश' (Satya Prakash) पत्रिका की शुरुआत की थी?
o: Karsondas Mulji
Vishnu Shastri Pandit
Veerasalingam Pantulu
B.M. Malabari
e: Detailed Explanation: Karsondas Mulji was a pioneering reformer who used journalism for social change. In 1852, he launched the Gujarati weekly 'Satya Prakash' to challenge orthodox practices and advocate for widow remarriage in western India.

qe: Professor D.K. Karve made outstanding structural contributions to the upliftment of high-caste Hindu widows in western India. Which practical measure did he initiate in Poona?
qh: प्रोफेसर डी.के. कर्वे ने पश्चिमी भारत में उच्च जाति की हिंदू विधवाओं के उत्थान में उत्कृष्ट योगदान दिया। उन्होंने पूना में कौन सा व्यावहारिक कदम शुरू किया?
o: He opened a dedicated widows' home providing facilities for vocational training
He introduced an aggressive legal suit inside the local high court against the priestly class
He completely banned the entry of lower castes into local standard schooling spaces
He established the first native maritime shipping company managed by women
e: Detailed Explanation: Professor D.K. Karve dedicated his life to the welfare of widows. He opened a widows' home in Poona to provide high-caste widows with shelter, education, and vocational training, helping them achieve independence and purpose.

qe: The Native Marriage Act (or Civil Marriage Act) of 1872 introduced legislative restrictions against child marriage, but it had a limited impact across India because:
qh: 1872 के नेटिव मैरिज एक्ट (या सिविल मैरिज एक्ट) ने बाल विवाह के खिलाफ विधायी प्रतिबंध पेश किए, लेकिन भारत भर में इसका सीमित प्रभाव पड़ा क्योंकि:
o: The Act was explicitly not applicable to Hindus, Muslims, and other recognized mainstream faiths
The colonial judiciary struck down the entire regulation as unconstitutional within a year
It raised the legal marriage age artificially to an unmanageable baseline of 25 years
The law was enforceable only within the remote limits of the Madras Presidency
e: Detailed Explanation: The Native Marriage Act of 1872 prohibited child marriage and permitted inter-caste marriages, but its scope was extremely narrow because it did not apply to Hindus, Muslims, or other major established religious faiths.

qe: The relentless efforts of the Parsi reformer B.M. Malabari directly culminated in the enactment of which piece of colonial legislation that prohibited the marriage of girls below the age of 12?
qh: पारसी सुधारक बी.एम. मालाबारी के अथक प्रयासों के परिणामस्वरूप कौन सा औपनिवेशिक कानून लागू हुआ, जिसने 12 वर्ष से कम उम्र की लड़कियों के विवाह को प्रतिबंधित कर दिया?
o: Age of Consent Act, 1891
Sarda Act, 1930
Native Marriage Act, 1872
Child Marriage Restraint Amendment Act, 1978
e: Detailed Explanation: B.M. Malabari campaigned vigorously against child marriage and the treatment of child widows. His efforts led to the passage of the Age of Consent Act in 1891, which raised the legal age of consent for marriage for girls to 12 years.

qe: The highly influential Sarda Act of 1930 pushed up the minimum legal marriage age boundaries across British India to which standard parameters?
qh: 1930 के अत्यधिक प्रभावशाली शारदा अधिनियम (Sarda Act) ने ब्रिटिश भारत में न्यूनतम कानूनी विवाह आयु सीमा को बढ़ाकर कितना कर दिया था?
o: 18 years for boys and 14 years for girls
21 years for boys and 18 years for girls
16 years for boys and 12 years for girls
20 years for boys and 15 years for girls
e: Detailed Explanation: The Child Marriage Restraint Act of 1929 (popularly known as the Sarda Act after its sponsor Rai Sahib Harbilas Sarda), which came into effect in 1930, fixed the minimum legal marriage age at 18 years for boys and 14 years for girls.

qe: Which educational institution, established in Calcutta in 1849, is recognized as the first major fruit of the powerful movement for women's higher education in India?
qh: 1849 में कलकत्ता में स्थापित कौन सा शैक्षणिक संस्थान, भारत में महिलाओं की उच्च शिक्षा के शक्तिशाली आंदोलन के पहले प्रमुख परिणाम के रूप में मान्यता प्राप्त है?
o: The Bethune School, founded by J.E.D. Bethune
The Calcutta Female Juvenile Society
The Lady Hardinge Medical College
The Indian Women’s University
e: Detailed Explanation: The Bethune School, founded in 1849 by John Elliot Drinkwater Bethune (President of the Council of Education), was a milestone. It was the first secular school for girls in India and triggered a broader movement for female education.

qe: Apart from his pioneering role in scriptural analysis for widow remarriage, Pandit Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was actively associated as an organizer with how many girls' schools in Bengal?
qh: विधवा पुनर्विवाह के लिए शास्त्रीय विश्लेषण में अपनी अग्रणी भूमिका के अलावा, पंडित ईश्वर चंद्र विद्यासागर बंगाल में कितने लड़कियों के स्कूलों के आयोजक के रूप में सक्रिय रूप से जुड़े हुए थे?
o: No less than 35 girls' schools
Exactly 5 girls' schools
More than 100 girls' schools
Strictly 12 girls' schools
e: Detailed Explanation: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a passionate advocate for female literacy. In his capacity as a government inspector of schools, he used his position and personal funds to organize and establish no less than 35 girls' schools across Bengal.

qe: Which landmark historical document on educational policy explicitly laid great structural stress on the urgent need for female education in British India in 1854?
qh: शिक्षा नीति पर किस ऐतिहासिक दस्तावेज़ ने 1854 में ब्रिटिश भारत में महिला शिक्षा की तत्काल आवश्यकता पर विशेष संरचनात्मक बल दिया था?
o: Charles Wood’s Despatch on Education
Macaulay’s Minute on Indian Education
The Hunter Commission Report
The Raleigh University Commission Guidelines
e: Detailed Explanation: Sir Charles Wood's Despatch on Education of 1854, often called the 'Magna Carta of English Education in India', explicitly highlighted the importance of female education and recommended government grants to support girls' schools.

qe: The outstanding institution known as the 'Indian Women’s University', which provided specialized higher education infrastructure to women, was set up in 1916 by which reformer?
qh: महिलाओं को विशेष उच्च शिक्षा बुनियादी ढांचा प्रदान करने वाले 'इंडियन विमेंस यूनिवर्सिटी' (Indian Women's University) की स्थापना 1916 में किस सुधारक द्वारा की गई थी?
o: Professor D.K. Karve
Ramabai Ranade
Sarla Devi Chaudhurani
Pandita Ramabai Saraswati
e: Detailed Explanation: In 1916, Professor D.K. Karve established the Indian Women's University (now known as SNDT Women's University) in Pune, marking a historic milestone as the first university dedicated exclusively to women in India.

qe: During the opening decades of the twentieth century, which mass political events served as the primary liberating experience for otherwise home-centered Indian women?
qh: बीसवीं शताब्दी के शुरुआती दशकों के दौरान, किन जन-राजनीतिक घटनाओं ने मुख्य रूप से घरेलू स्तर पर केंद्रित भारतीय महिलाओं के लिए प्राथमिक मुक्ति के अनुभव के रूप में कार्य किया?
o: Participation in the Swadeshi, anti-partition, and Home Rule movements
Attending secret commercial banking tracking seminars in Bombay
Filing joint civil lawsuits against local village panchayats
Enrolling into newly opened British military administrative services
e: Detailed Explanation: Entering the public sphere during the Swadeshi (1905), anti-partition, and Home Rule movements marked a major turning point for Indian women. They stepped out of domestic isolation to join processions, picket shops, and engage in political activism.

qe: The organization named 'Bharat Stree Mahamandal', which held its first historical meeting in Allahabad in 1910, was founded by which prominent woman leader?
qh: 1910 में इलाहाबाद में अपनी पहली ऐतिहासिक बैठक आयोजित करने वाले 'भारत स्त्री महामंडल' (Bharat Stree Mahamandal) नामक संगठन की स्थापना किस प्रमुख महिला नेता द्वारा की गई थी?
o: Sarla Devi Chaudhurani
Ramabai Ranade
Pandita Ramabai
Sarojini Naidu
e: Detailed Explanation: Sarla Devi Chaudhurani convened the first meeting of the Bharat Stree Mahamandal in Allahabad in 1910. It is widely considered the first major pan-Indian women's organization established by a woman, aimed at promoting female education and abolishing the purdah system.

qe: The prominent 'Ladies Social Conference' (Bharat Mahila Parishad) was founded in 1904 in Bombay as a specialized wing under the structural guidance of which parent body?
qh: प्रसिद्ध 'लेडीज सोशल कॉन्फ्रेंस' (भारत महिला परिषद) की स्थापना 1904 में बॉम्बे में किस मूल संस्था के संरचनात्मक मार्गदर्शन में एक विशेष शाखा के रूप में की गई थी?
o: The National Social Conference
The Brahmo Samaj Core Council
The Arya Mahila Samaj
The All India Women’s Conference
e: Detailed Explanation: Ramabai Ranade founded the Ladies Social Conference (Bharat Mahila Parishad) in 1904 in Bombay. It operated as a specialized branch under the aegis of the National Social Conference, focusing on targeted social reforms for women.

qe: The 'All India Women’s Conference' (AIWC), recognized as one of the first major women's organizations with an egalitarian approach, was founded in 1927 by whom?
qh: एक समतावादी दृष्टिकोण (egalitarian approach) के साथ पहले प्रमुख महिला संगठनों में से एक के रूप में मान्यता प्राप्त 'अखिल भारतीय महिला सम्मेलन' (AIWC) की स्थापना 1927 में किसके द्वारा की गई थी?
o: Margaret Cousins
Sarla Devi Chaudhurani
Mehribai Tata
Cornelia Sorabji
e: Detailed Explanation: The All India Women’s Conference (AIWC) was founded by Margaret Cousins in 1927. Its first conference was hosted at Fergusson College, Pune, with founding members including Sarojini Naidu and Kamladevi Chattopadhyaya.

qe: Which of the following objective principles formed the core constitutional vision of the All India Women’s Conference (AIWC) when it expanded its platform in 1927?
qh: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा उद्देश्य सिद्धांत अखिल भारतीय महिला सम्मेलन (AIWC) के मुख्य संवैधानिक दृष्टिकोण का हिस्सा था जब उसने 1927 में अपने मंच का विस्तार किया था?
o: To work for a society based on principles of social justice, integrity, equal rights, and opportunities
To enforce the strict insulation of intermediate caste tracking across legislatures
To structurally support the retention of the medieval purdah status systems
To dynamically channelize land ownership exclusively to wealthy banking families
e: Detailed Explanation: The AIWC was built on an egalitarian philosophy. Its stated goals were to fight for a society rooted in social justice, integrity, equal rights, and opportunities, ensuring the essentials of life were distributed based on fairness rather than accident of birth or sex.

qe: The rigid structural concept of Hindu 'chaturvarnashrama' dictated that a person's caste status systematically determined which social privileges before birth?
qh: हिंदू 'चातुर्वर्णश्रम' की कठोर संरचनात्मक अवधारणा यह निर्देशित करती थी कि किसी व्यक्ति की जाति की स्थिति जन्म से पहले ही किन सामाजिक विशेषाधिकारों को व्यवस्थित रूप से निर्धारित करती थी?
o: Access to education, land ownership, profession, and sources of drinking water
The precise volume of international maritime import trade parameters
Direct baseline tracking metrics of judicial high court appeals
The structural layout of currency print velocity values inside local markets
e: Detailed Explanation: Under the rigid chaturvarnashrama framework, caste dictated almost every aspect of an individual's social life before birth—including access to education, ownership of landed property, professional pursuits, sources of drinking water, and temple entry rules.

qe: How did the introduction of British administrative and legal measures indirectly deal a severe blow to traditional caste-based inequalities in India?
qh: ब्रिटिश प्रशासनिक और कानूनी उपायों की शुरूआत ने अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से भारत में पारंपरिक जाति-आधारित असमानताओं को कैसे गहरा झटका दिया?
o: By introducing the concept of equality before law in a uniformly applied system of law and stripping caste panchayats of judicial functions
By legally forcing all intermediate castes to engage in uniform agricultural vocations
By mandating that scriptural studies must be cleared by British military tribunals
By entirely freezing urban mobility and eliminating private property in land
e: Detailed Explanation: The British administration introduced a uniform legal system based on the principle of equality before the law. By removing judicial powers from traditional caste panchayats and opening administrative services to all castes on secular lines, it structurally undermined old caste hierarchies.

qe: Mahatma Gandhi launched a comprehensive national crusade to eradicate untouchability root and branch. Which specialized organization did he establish in 1932 to advance this cause?
qh: महात्मा गांधी ने अस्पृश्यता को जड़ से खत्म करने के लिए एक व्यापक राष्ट्रीय अभियान शुरू किया। इस उद्देश्य को आगे बढ़ाने के लिए उन्होंने 1932 में किस विशेष संगठन की स्थापना की?
o: All India Harijan Sangh
Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha
All India Scheduled Castes Federation
Self-Respect Movement Front
e: Detailed Explanation: Anchoring his campaign on humanism and reason, Mahatma Gandhi founded the All India Harijan Sangh in 1932 to combat untouchability and launched the weekly publication 'Harijan' to advocate for the civil rights of the depressed classes.

qe: In Maharashtra, the powerful anti-caste movement challenging Brahminical domination and prioritizing lower-caste and female literacy was spearheaded by which iconic reformer?
qh: महाराष्ट्र में, ब्राह्मणवादी वर्चस्व को चुनौती देने वाले और निचली जाति तथा महिला साक्षरता को प्राथमिकता देने वाले शक्तिशाली जाति-विरोधी आंदोलन का नेतृत्व किस प्रसिद्ध सुधारक ने किया था?
o: Jyotiba Phule
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
The Maharaja of Kolhapur
Ramabai Ranade
e: Detailed Explanation: Jyotiba Phule, born into a low-caste Mali family, led a historic movement against upper-caste hegemony in Maharashtra. He prioritized education for the lower strata and established several pioneering schools for girls and lower-caste children.

qe: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar led the historic 'Mahad Satyagraha' in March 1927. What specific civil right was targeted during this public demonstration?
qh: डॉ. बी.आर. अंबेडकर ने मार्च 1927 में ऐतिहासिक 'महाद सत्याग्रह' (Mahad Satyagraha) का नेतृत्व किया था। इस सार्वजनिक प्रदर्शन के दौरान किस विशिष्ट नागरिक अधिकार को लक्षित किया गया था?
o: The right of untouchables to draw water from the public Chawdar tank
Securing separate political representation parameters inside local district boards
Forcing the colonial judiciary to completely ban the free sale of land
Demanding the immediate closure of all high-cost British educational facilities
e: Detailed Explanation: The Mahad Satyagraha of March 1927 was an iconic civil rights campaign led by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. He led a procession of thousands of untouchables to the Chawdar tank in Mahad to assert their right to use a public water source that had historically been denied to them by orthodox caste groups.

qe: The specialized organization named 'Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha', which operated under the transformative motto 'Educate, Agitate and Organise', was established in 1924 by whom?
qh: परिवर्तनकारी आदर्श वाक्य 'शिक्षित करो, संघर्ष करो और संगठित बनो' (Educate, Agitate and Organise) के तहत काम करने वाले 'बहिष्कृत हितकारिणी सभा' (Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha) की स्थापना 1924 में किसके द्वारा की गई थी?
o: Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar
Jyotiba Phule
E.V. Ramaswamy Naicker
Sri Narayana Guru
e: Detailed Explanation: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar founded the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha in Bombay in 1924. The organization was designed to bring the grievances of Dalits to the government's attention, promote education, and improve their socio-economic conditions under the banner: 'Educate, Agitate and Organise'.
